hero.headline: Key U.S. spy authority nears expiration as lawmakers warn of national security risk
hero.teaser: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act could lapse on Friday, threatening intelligence operations.
hero.body:
One of America's most powerful spy authorities is nearing an unprecedented lapse, threatening to plunge intelligence agencies and telecommunications companies into legal uncertainty if allowed to expire on Friday. Members in both parties are warning that an expiration of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act could jeopardize U.S. national security.

Section 702 feeds more than half of the president's daily briefing and has been credited with helping thwart terror plots and other national security threats. The looming expiration adds pressure to lawmakers already dealing with uncertainty in the intelligence community.

cards.headline: U.S. conducts second night of airstrikes on Iran
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military launched strikes on Iran for the second consecutive evening on Wednesday, escalating military operations against Tehran. U.S. officials said the intent was to pressure Iran to sign a deal, though the strikes also carry a risk of further military escalation.

U.S. officials said they expected an Iranian response, possibly targeting U.S. bases, as happened on Tuesday. Tehran announced Wednesday night that its military had targeted the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet in Bahrain with drones in response to the latest American strikes, though it was not immediately clear whether the attack had struck its target.

The strikes mark a significant intensification of military action between the two nations. The two-night campaign represents the most direct U.S. military action against Iranian territory in recent years, raising questions about whether the situation will continue to escalate or whether the pressure will bring Iran to the negotiating table.

The dual-pronged approach by U.S. officials—conducting military strikes while simultaneously stating they aim to achieve a diplomatic agreement—reflects the tension between coercive tactics and the desire to avoid a broader regional conflict. The strikes come at a time when U.S. forces maintain a significant presence in the Middle East, including the 5th Fleet headquarters in Bahrain.

The situation continues to develop as both nations assess the impacts of the latest exchanges. U.S. officials indicated they are monitoring for further Iranian responses while maintaining their stated objective of reaching a negotiated settlement.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as U.S. and Iran Exchange Fire for Second Day
cards.teaser: Oil markets reacted to escalating military conflict between the United States and Iran, raising fears of prolonged confrontation.
cards.body:
Oil prices jumped as the United States and Iran exchanged strikes for a second consecutive day. Iran responded to U.S. attacks on multiple Iranian cities by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, with damage reported in Bahrain's capital.

The escalating hostilities have intensified concerns about regional stability and energy supplies. Negotiations to end the conflict remain stalled, with Iran maintaining control over the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments.

cards.headline: Consumer Prices Rise 4.2% in May, Highest Inflation Rate in Three Years
cards.body:
Consumer prices climbed to an annual rate of 4.2 percent in May, the highest level in three years, as conflict in the Middle East pushed energy costs higher and contributed to broader price increases across the economy. The inflation reading represents the third consecutive monthly jump since the Iran war began.

The sharp acceleration in inflation comes as disruptions to global energy markets have driven up oil prices. Before the conflict started, inflation was running at 2.4 percent. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has been a major factor in rising energy costs worldwide.

Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, climbed to $111.16 per barrel early in the trading week, its highest level in nearly two weeks. The price surge followed an attack on a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates and stalled peace negotiations between the United States and Iran.

President Trump responded to the inflation report on Wednesday, saying "I love the inflation" and indicating he was not concerned about the price increases given recent developments in the conflict.

The elevated inflation figures have reverberated across global financial markets. Government bond yields have risen sharply in response to inflation concerns and expectations that central banks will need to increase interest rates. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield hit 4.631 percent, its highest level since February 2025. In the United Kingdom, the 10-year gilt yield surpassed an 18-year high, reaching 5.19 percent before pulling back slightly.

Stock markets opened lower across major regions on Monday in response to the geopolitical tensions and inflation worries. Europe's Stoxx 600 index dropped 0.7 percent, while Japan's Nikkei fell about 1 percent. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index also declined 1 percent.

Meanwhile, finance ministers from the G7 nations gathered in Paris to discuss the economic effects of the Middle East conflict. In Japan, the government prepared to issue fresh debt as part of an effort to cushion the economic impact from the war.

Bond market volatility has also been influenced by political developments in the United Kingdom, where traders are anticipating potential leadership changes that could affect fiscal policy. However, some analysts suggested that if investors believe spending pressures will be controlled, bond yields could begin to retreat.

Economists and policymakers are closely monitoring whether the inflation spike proves temporary or signals a sustained period of elevated prices. The data will shape monetary policy decisions in coming months as central banks balance the need to control inflation against risks to economic growth.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi visits North Korea amid regional tensions
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping traveled to Pyongyang for talks with Kim Jong Un, with both nations claiming diplomatic wins from the meeting.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Pyongyang for a two-day visit, his first to North Korea in nearly seven years. Xi traveled with his wife, Peng Liyuan, aboard an Air China plane to the country's capital. The trip marks a significant effort by China to strengthen its relationship with North Korea, particularly as tensions have strained their alliance due to Pyongyang's growing closeness with Russia.

During the visit, Xi notably refrained from publicly addressing North Korea's nuclear program, even as Kim Jong Un emphasized the irreversibility of his country's status as a nuclear power. Both governments characterized the diplomatic engagement as successful, though analysts observed that fundamental limitations continue to define their relationship.

cards.headline: Atlantic Ocean Cold Spot Suggests Major Current System May Be Weakening
cards.teaser: Scientists say an anomalous cold region in the Atlantic could signal changes to ocean circulation patterns.
cards.body:
Researchers have identified a persistent cold region in the Atlantic Ocean that may indicate the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is approaching a tipping point. The AMOC is a system of ocean currents that moves warm water northward and cold water southward, influencing weather patterns across multiple continents.

The cold spot appears anomalous because ocean temperatures are rising globally due to climate change. Scientists say the cooler water could result from a slowdown in the circulation system, which would have significant implications for weather in North America and Europe. The AMOC has weakened in recent decades, and some climate models suggest further decline could trigger abrupt shifts in regional climates.

cards.headline: Amnesty International accuses Israel of ethnic cleansing in West Bank
cards.teaser: The human rights organization says the Israeli government is deliberately attempting to annex Palestinian territory.
cards.body:
Amnesty International has accused the Israeli government of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, claiming officials are deliberately attempting to annex Palestinian territory. The London-based human rights organization released the report as part of ongoing international scrutiny of Israeli policies in the occupied region.

This marks the latest in a series of critical assessments from Amnesty International regarding the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The organization has previously issued reports examining actions by both Israeli and Palestinian authorities in the area.

hero.headline: Ukraine war surpasses World War I in duration
hero.teaser: The conflict in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, which spanned from 1914 to 1918.
hero.body:
The war in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, surpassing a conflict that defined an era. What began as a planned three-day invasion has instead evolved into a protracted military struggle that has defied initial expectations.

The extended conflict has drawn comparisons to the First World War, with observers noting similarities in the grinding nature of combat and the role of new technologies in transforming how battles are fought. The prolonged fighting has reshaped Ukrainian society and raised concerns about global stability.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi visits North Korea amid regional tensions
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping traveled to Pyongyang for talks with Kim Jong Un, with both nations claiming diplomatic wins from the meeting.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Pyongyang for a two-day visit, his first to North Korea in nearly seven years. Xi traveled with his wife, Peng Liyuan, aboard an Air China plane to the country's capital. The trip marks a significant effort by China to strengthen its relationship with North Korea, particularly as tensions have strained their alliance due to Pyongyang's growing closeness with Russia.

cards.headline: South Korea fines major e-commerce company record $409 million
cards.teaser: Coupang, a US-incorporated e-commerce giant operating in South Korea, faces the country's largest regulatory fine.
cards.body:
South Korean regulators imposed a record $409 million fine on Coupang, an e-commerce company incorporated in the United States but operating primarily in South Korea. The penalty represents the largest such action by Korean authorities against a major online retailer.

The investigation and resulting fine have created diplomatic friction between Seoul and Washington. Coupang's dual status as a US-incorporated company serving the Korean market has complicated the regulatory action, with the substantial penalty drawing attention from American officials concerned about treatment of US-based firms.

cards.headline: Violence erupts in Belfast with police injured in clashes
cards.teaser: Twelve police officers were injured during a second night of disorder in Belfast, with water cannons deployed against crowds.
cards.body:
Police in Belfast faced a second night of violent disorder as protesters set fires and threw bricks and bottles. Twelve officers sustained injuries during the clashes, prompting authorities to deploy water cannons near the city center to disperse crowds.

The unrest followed a stabbing incident and has been characterized by anti-immigrant sentiment. A nurse was chased into a hospital by masked individuals during the violence. The disorder reflects renewed communal tensions in Northern Ireland, drawing comparisons to the region's history of sectarian conflict.

cards.headline: French singer Patrick Bruel under formal investigation for rape
cards.teaser: The French entertainer was released under judicial supervision while magistrates examine the allegations.
cards.body:
French singer Patrick Bruel has been charged with rape and sexual assault following a formal investigation. The 67-year-old was released from custody and placed under judicial supervision while an examining magistrate conducts a deeper examination of the case. Bruel has denied all charges against him.

The charges relate to four separate cases involving alleged rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment. More than 20 women have made allegations against the musician dating back to the 1990s, making this one of the most significant MeToo cases in the French music industry.

cards.headline: World Cup begins amid strained North American relations
cards.teaser: The tournament kicks off with Mexico, Canada, and the United States as co-hosts despite recent diplomatic tensions.
cards.body:
The World Cup opened with a historic three-nation hosting arrangement involving the United States, Mexico, and Canada. Mexico and Canada have both faced recent tensions in their relationships with Washington.

Despite these diplomatic challenges, the three countries have publicly promoted cooperation and teamwork throughout their joint hosting effort. The tournament represents a significant test of regional collaboration during a period of political friction between the North American neighbors.

cards.headline: South Korea's chip industry inspires new workplace slang
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence boom has supercharged South Korea's semiconductor sector, generating fresh cultural terminology.
cards.body:
South Korea's semiconductor industry has flourished amid growing demand for chips powering artificial intelligence. The boom has reshaped workplace culture, generating new slang terms and memes that reflect the sector's prominence in the country's economy.

"Silicon-collar" is among the emerging vocabulary connected to the chip industry's expansion. These linguistic innovations underscore how deeply the semiconductor boom has embedded itself into South Korean society and popular culture.

hero.headline: US military strikes oil tanker, killing three Indian sailors
hero.teaser: The US military attacked a Palau-flagged oil tanker after accusing the vessel of failing to comply with directions.
hero.body:
The US military attacked the Palau-flagged tanker Settebello off the coast of Oman on Wednesday, accusing it of not complying with directions. Three Indian sailors were killed in the strike. India's government said 21 crew members were rescued following the attack.

The strike was part of escalating military operations in the Middle East, where the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the second consecutive day. Iran responded by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain, with reported damage to Bahrain's capital city.

cards.headline: Knicks rally from 29 points down to take 3-1 lead in NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks completed a record comeback from 29 points down to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 on Wednesday night, moving within one game of their .
cards.body:
The New York Knicks mounted a historic comeback from 29 points down to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 on Wednesday night. The victory puts the Knicks one win away from their first championship since 1973.

The remarkable rally represents a record comeback in NBA Finals history. With a 3-1 series lead, the Knicks now have multiple opportunities to clinch the title and end their 50-year championship drought.

cards.headline: Amnesty International accuses Israel of ethnic cleansing in West Bank
cards.teaser: The human rights organization says the Israeli government is deliberately attempting to annex Palestinian territory.
cards.body:
Amnesty International has accused the Israeli government of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, claiming officials are deliberately attempting to annex Palestinian territory. The London-based human rights organization released the report as part of ongoing international scrutiny of Israeli policies in the occupied region.

This marks the latest in a series of critical assessments from Amnesty International regarding the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The organization has previously issued reports examining actions by both Israeli and Palestinian authorities in the area.

cards.headline: Police use water cannons on protesters during second night of Belfast unrest
cards.teaser: Violence erupted for a second night in Northern Ireland following a stabbing incident that sparked anti-immigrant demonstrations.
cards.body:
Police deployed water cannons against protesters during a second night of violence in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Demonstrators set small fires and threw bricks and bottles at officers.

The unrest was sparked by a stabbing incident in the city, which triggered anti-immigrant protests in the region.

cards.headline: UK regulator investigates Ryanair over child seating charges
cards.teaser: The competition authority is examining fees the airline imposes on parents who want to sit next to their children.
cards.body:
The UK's competition regulator is investigating Ryanair over charges the airline imposes on parents who want to sit next to their children.

The probe will examine whether these fees comply with consumer protection standards in the UK.

cards.headline: London police chief calls for legislation to disable stolen phones
cards.teaser: Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley asked the home secretary to require tech companies to publish data on stolen devices.
cards.body:
Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley has called on the home secretary to introduce new legislation that would force technology companies to make stolen phones unusable. He also wants firms to publish data on stolen devices as part of efforts to tackle phone theft in London.

The request represents law enforcement's push to gain additional tools in combating the issue of mobile phone theft across the capital.

cards.headline: Pope Leo travels to Canary Islands to address migrant crisis
cards.teaser: The pontiff will appeal for humane treatment of migrants seeking better lives during his visit to the Spanish territory.
cards.body:
Pope Leo is traveling to the Canary Islands to draw attention to the dangerous journeys migrants undertake while seeking to reach Europe. The visit underscores the perilous routes faced by people attempting to improve their lives.

During his time there, the Pope will call for migrants to be treated with humanity and welcomed with respect. The Canary Islands serve as a major gateway for migrants traveling from Africa to European territory.

cards.headline: South Korea Fines E-Commerce Giant Coupang $409 Million Over Data Breach
cards.teaser: The record fine follows a massive data breach that exposed private information of approximately 37.5 million users.
cards.body:
South Korea's financial regulator has fined Coupang $400 million for a data breach that compromised personal information belonging to approximately 37.5 million users. The penalty marks the largest fine ever imposed for a data protection violation in the country.

Coupang, widely regarded as South Korea's equivalent to Amazon, faced the record sanction due to the scale of the incident and the sensitivity of the exposed user data. The hefty fine underscores regulators' commitment to holding major digital platforms accountable for safeguarding consumer privacy.

cards.headline: Oracle Reports Higher Profit on Cloud Revenue Growth
cards.teaser: Oracle beat earnings expectations but stock dropped as the company announced plans to raise an additional $20 billion.
cards.body:
Oracle reported higher quarterly profits driven by surging cloud revenue, beating earnings expectations in its latest financial results. The technology company has been undergoing a rapid transformation to expand its cloud computing business amid growing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Despite the positive earnings beat, Oracle's stock declined after the company revealed plans to raise another $20 billion. The company's AI spending has exceeded estimates, raising concerns among investors about growing debt levels as Oracle invests heavily in cloud infrastructure and AI capabilities.

cards.headline: European Central Bank Set to Raise Interest Rates as Inflation Rises
cards.teaser: The ECB is preparing its first rate increase since September 2023 as energy disruptions drive higher prices.
cards.body:
The European Central Bank is preparing to raise interest rates for the first time since September 2023 as inflationary pressures mount across the continent. The rate increase reflects broader global inflation concerns, with the Iran conflict disrupting energy supplies and driving up prices.

Central banks face a difficult balancing act between controlling inflation and supporting economic growth during a period of geopolitical instability. The ECB's decision signals policymakers' commitment to addressing price increases even as higher energy costs risk slowing the broader economy.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as U.S. and Iran Exchange Fire for Second Day
cards.teaser: Oil markets reacted to escalating military conflict between the United States and Iran, raising fears of prolonged confrontation.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall on Inflation and Geopolitical Concerns
cards.teaser: Major U.S. stock indexes declined more than 1 percent as investors weighed inflation data and Iran conflict risks.
cards.body:
Wall Street indexes fell more than 1 percent as investors reacted to rising inflation figures and ongoing geopolitical tensions. The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 950 points to close below the 50,000 mark, while the S&P 500 fell 1.6 percent and the Nasdaq tumbled 2 percent.

Technology stocks led the decline amid broader concerns about inflation, the Iran conflict, and market valuations. Investors are reassessing risk as economic data shows accelerating price pressures and geopolitical uncertainties cloud the outlook for corporate earnings and economic growth.

cards.headline: Medicare Advantage Plans Frequently Deny Seniors Special Care Access
cards.teaser: Two government reports show Medicare Advantage insurers are quick to reject requests for nursing home and rehabilitation services.
cards.body:
Medicare Advantage plans are frequently denying seniors access to short-term nursing home care and inpatient rehabilitation services, according to two reports by U.S. investigators. The analysis reveals systematic patterns of claim rejections that limit access to specialized care for elderly patients.

The findings raise questions about how Medicare Advantage insurers manage care authorization and whether coverage limitations are inappropriately restricting medically necessary services. The reports provide new evidence in ongoing debates about the quality and accessibility of care under Medicare Advantage compared to traditional Medicare.

hero.headline: Apple Updates Siri With Contextual Awareness and Silence Detection
hero.body:
Apple introduced a substantially redesigned Siri at its Worldwide Developers Conference 2026, marking a major shift in the voice assistant's capabilities and architecture. The new version, now called Siri AI, integrates with Apple Intelligence and will be available to all users in the fall as part of iOS 27.

The revamp represents a fundamental departure from Siri's previous design. Rather than functioning primarily as a web-based question-and-answer tool, the new Siri operates as a conversational AI assistant similar to ChatGPT and Google Gemini. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, explained that the tool has been rebuilt with generative AI at its core, powered by Google's Gemini model through a billion-dollar partnership between the two companies.

One of the most significant improvements is Siri's ability to recognize when users have finished speaking. The assistant can now detect pauses in conversation and determine whether a user is simply taking a breath or has completed their thought. This contextual awareness allows Siri to respond at appropriate moments rather than interrupting prematurely, making interactions feel more natural and less mechanical.

The new Siri will function as a dedicated app capable of drawing information from Apple's native ecosystem across mobile devices and laptops. In a demonstration, Rockwell showed how the assistant could identify a location from a photo, retrieve a friend's address from contacts, and provide directions with a planned stop, all within a single interface. Beyond navigation, the app will handle proofreading, shopping, calendar management, and image analysis such as retrieving nutritional information from photos of food. Initially, the service will be available only in English.

Apple also announced expanded child safety features alongside the Siri update. The company introduced new parental controls that limit content visibility, restrict communication contacts, and regulate app access. A new setup assistant helps parents customize restrictions and gradually expand access as children age. Additional features include requiring permission before accessing new websites in Safari and proactively monitoring messages for violent or graphic content.

The announcements reflect Apple's broader effort to catch up in the AI race. Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice-president of software engineering, acknowledged the company's previous lag in AI development compared to competitors. Apple has repeatedly delayed previous Siri updates originally announced in 2024, and the company settled a 250 million dollar class-action lawsuit in May over false advertising of Siri's capabilities.

The new Siri represents the third generation of Apple's foundation models and will integrate AI features into Safari, messaging, the Home app, and camera tools. All updates will roll out as part of the next operating system releases, with developers receiving preview access at the conference.

cards.headline: Engineer Sues xAI Over Alleged Firing for Safety Concerns About Grok
cards.teaser: A former xAI engineer claims he was fired after raising safety concerns about the Grok AI system.
cards.body:
A former xAI engineer has sued the company and SpaceX, claiming he was fired for raising safety concerns about the Grok artificial intelligence system. According to the lawsuit, the termination occurred days before SpaceX's initial public offering.

The engineer alleged he flagged issues related to AI safety protocols while employed at xAI. Both xAI and SpaceX are named as defendants in the case.

cards.headline: Ubisoft Closes Studios in San Francisco and Winnipeg, Affecting 380 Employees
cards.teaser: The gaming company is shuttering multiple offices as part of an organizational restructuring.
cards.body:
Ubisoft announced the closure of studios in San Francisco and Winnipeg as part of a broader restructuring that could affect approximately 380 employees. The Winnipeg office employed about 65 people before the closure decision.

The company described the moves as part of organizational changes intended to streamline operations. Ubisoft has faced financial pressure in recent quarters, leading to cost-cutting measures across its global studio network. The closures add to a wave of layoffs that have affected the video game industry over the past two years.

cards.headline: Framework Delays Laptop 13 Pro Shipments by One Month Due to Software Issues
cards.teaser: The modular laptop maker pushed back delivery dates to July to address bugs in the new model.
cards.body:
Framework has postponed the initial shipments of its Laptop 13 Pro by one month, pushing the launch from June to July. The company noted that some orders may experience further delays extending into early August.

The Laptop 13 Pro represents Framework's flagship 13-inch model, featuring the company's signature modular design that allows users to upgrade individual components. Framework is compensating customers for the extended wait by including additional features with their orders.

cards.headline: Venus and Jupiter Appear Close Together in Night Sky During Planetary Conjunction
cards.teaser: The two brightest planets aligned in a visible conjunction that peaked on June 9.
cards.body:
Venus and Jupiter appeared unusually close together in the night sky during a planetary conjunction that reached its closest point on June 9. The alignment allowed observers to see both planets near each other in the dusk sky, creating what astronomers call a conjunction.

Conjunctions occur when planets appear to pass near each other from Earth's perspective, though they remain millions of miles apart in space. Venus and Jupiter are the two brightest planets visible from Earth, making their alignment particularly striking to casual observers. Photographers captured images of the event from various locations around the world.

cards.headline: Extreme Rainfall Killed 7 Percent of Tapanuli Orangutans, Study Finds
cards.teaser: Four days of intense rain caused deaths among the world's rarest orangutan population.
cards.body:
A study has found that extreme rainfall in Indonesia's North Sumatra province killed approximately 7 percent of the world's remaining Tapanuli orangutans. More than 1,000mm of rain fell over four days in November 2025, triggering landslides that killed an estimated 58 individuals out of the species' total population of around 800.

The deaths represent 11 percent of the local population and underscore the vulnerability of the critically endangered species. Researchers attribute the intense weather event to the climate crisis, warning that such extreme rainfall events pose direct and immediate threats to the orangutans' survival.

hero.headline: Tharp breaks 110m hurdles world record at US college championships
hero.body:
Ja'Kobe Tharp broke the 110-meter hurdles world record during heats at the American college championships on Wednesday. The performance marked a historic achievement in track and field, surpassing the previous global standard in one of the sport's premier sprinting events.

The record fell during preliminary rounds of the competition, demonstrating Tharp's exceptional form early in the meet. Breaking a world record in a heat rather than a final is unusual, as athletes typically reserve their peak performances for medal rounds. Tharp's time eclipsed the previous mark, establishing him as the fastest hurdler in history over the distance.

The 110-meter hurdles is one of track and field's most technical events, requiring athletes to maintain sprinting speed while clearing ten barriers spaced precisely along the track. World records in the event are rare, with previous marks standing for years before being broken. Tharp's achievement at the college level underscores the depth of talent in American collegiate athletics.

The American college championships serve as the culminating event of the NCAA outdoor track season, bringing together the nation's top collegiate athletes. Many Olympic medalists and professional track stars have emerged from the meet, which features competition across sprints, distance races, jumps, and throws. Tharp's record-breaking performance will likely elevate his profile ahead of future international competitions.

The breakthrough adds to what has been a competitive season in men's hurdles, with several athletes posting fast times throughout the spring. Tharp now holds the fastest time ever recorded in the event, positioning him as a favorite for major championships. His performance will be officially ratified by World Athletics, the sport's governing body, which reviews all world record claims before confirming them in the official record books.

cards.headline: Knicks rally from 29 points down to take 3-1 NBA Finals lead over Spurs
cards.teaser: New York overcame a historic deficit in Game 4, moving within one win of the franchise's first championship since 1973.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks erased a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, achieving the largest comeback in NBA Finals history. OG Anunoby's tip-in with 1.2 seconds remaining off a missed Jalen Brunson three-pointer secured the victory and gave New York a commanding 3-1 series lead.

The Knicks are now one win away from their first NBA championship in 53 years. The dramatic turnaround unfolded in front of a stunned Madison Square Garden crowd as the team mounted an improbable fourth-quarter rally against San Antonio.

cards.headline: Mahomes set to become NFL's first $500 million player
cards.teaser: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is poised to reach the historic contract milestone.
cards.body:
Patrick Mahomes is set to become the first NFL player to sign a contract worth $500 million. Kansas City Chiefs owner Clark Hunt praised the quarterback as a "generational talent and elite human being," underscoring the organization's commitment to retaining him.

The record-breaking deal reflects Mahomes' status as one of professional football's most valuable players. His success with the Chiefs has established him among the league's elite quarterbacks.

cards.headline: Wolves dismiss head coach Edwards after seven months
cards.teaser: Wolverhampton Wanderers parted ways with Rob Edwards just months into his tenure.
cards.body:
Wolverhampton Wanderers have sacked head coach Rob Edwards after seven months in charge. Edwards, who was appointed last November on a three-and-a-half year deal, was unable to prevent the club's relegation from the Premier League. He took over with Wolves bottom of the league on two points from 11 matches and failed to improve their position significantly.

The club's poor form ultimately led to relegation in April, ending an eight-year spell in the top tier. Edwards' departure follows the earlier sacking of his predecessor Vítor Pereira. Wolves are now targeting Portuguese manager César Peixoto as a replacement.

cards.headline: UFC to host event at White House with fighters honoring Trump
cards.teaser: UFC Freedom 250 will take place at the White House in a historic first for the sport.
cards.body:
The UFC will hold its Freedom 250 event at the White House, marking the first time a mixed martial arts card has been staged at the executive mansion. Fighters said they were honored to compete in front of President Trump, who has maintained close ties to UFC leadership.

The event represents a significant departure from traditional White House sporting events. The full fight card, date, and broadcast details have been announced. Trump was described as an invisible guest as fighters arrived for the unprecedented competition, which blends sports and politics in a way rarely seen in American history.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Christie seeks World Cup history after Euro 2024 disappointment
cards.teaser: Ryan Christie said Scotland's painful European Championship campaign is fueling their World Cup qualifying push.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Ryan Christie said the team is using the disappointment of Euro 2024 as motivation to qualify for the World Cup. Christie described the national team as having a chip on its shoulder as it pursues a historic achievement in the global tournament.

Scotland's Euro 2024 campaign ended in disappointment, with the team failing to advance from the group stage. The squad is now focused on World Cup qualification, seeking to reach the tournament for the first time in years. Christie's comments reflect a determination to turn past failure into future success on the international stage.

cards.headline: Patriots open minicamp with Gonzalez and Boutte in attendance
cards.teaser: New England began its mandatory minicamp with key players reporting as the team addresses contract situations.
cards.body: The New England Patriots opened mandatory minicamp with cornerback Christian Gonzalez and wide receiver Kayshon Boutte present on the first day. Quarterback Drake Maye showed sharpness in practice, while Gonzalez participated after missing time earlier in the offseason. Day one featured a lighter schedule before the team's final push to conclude the offseason program. Maye has been working to build rapport with his receivers heading into the regular season.

hero.headline: K-pop Group BigBang Announces 31-Show World Tour for 20th Anniversary
hero.body:
K-pop group BigBang will reunite for a 31-show stadium world tour celebrating its 20th anniversary, marking the group's first tour since 2017. Members G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung announced the tour on Thursday, spanning seven months across multiple continents.

The tour will begin August 21 at Goyang Stadium in Goyang, South Korea, and continue through February 28, 2027. The group has scheduled performances across Asia, North America, and Europe, bringing their music to fans worldwide after a seven-year absence from touring.

BigBang originally debuted in 2006 and became one of the most influential acts in K-pop history. The group's hiatus from touring followed individual members pursuing solo projects and fulfilling mandatory military service requirements in South Korea. The reunion tour brings together three of the group's members for what represents a significant moment in K-pop, as one of the genre's pioneering acts returns to the stage.

The tour will play exclusively in stadium venues, reflecting the group's continued popularity despite the extended break from performing together. The 31-show run represents one of the larger touring commitments for a K-pop act, with dates spanning both the summer and winter seasons across two calendar years.

Ticketing information and specific cities for the tour dates have not yet been announced. The tour marks BigBang's return to the international stage at a time when K-pop has achieved unprecedented global reach, with the genre expanding significantly in the years since the group last toured together.

cards.headline: French Singer Patrick Bruel Under Investigation for Rape
cards.teaser: French singer Patrick Bruel was placed under formal investigation for rape and released from custody under judicial supervision.
cards.body:
French singer Patrick Bruel has been charged with rape and sexual assault following allegations from more than 20 women. The 67-year-old was placed under formal investigation for four cases involving alleged rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment dating back to the 1990s. Bruel has denied all charges.

The musician was released from custody under judicial supervision while an examining magistrate conducts a deeper investigation into the allegations. The case is among the largest MeToo cases in the French music industry.

cards.headline: Tony Leung Announces Three New Projects While Chairing Shanghai Jury
cards.teaser: Hong Kong actor Tony Leung Chiu-wai disclosed three upcoming productions while serving as jury president at the Shanghai International Film Festival.
cards.body:
Actor Tony Leung Chiu-wai announced three projects in development: a film directed by Johnnie To, a separate India-set production, and a streaming series where he will play a serial killer. The actor shared the information while speaking ahead of his role as jury president at an international film festival.

The streaming series will run six or seven episodes. Leung, known for his work in Hong Kong cinema, has not released additional details about production timelines or release dates for the three projects.

cards.headline: Celebrities Attend Knicks Game 4 at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift, Adam Sandler, Spike Lee, and other celebrities watched the New York Knicks play the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
A group of celebrities gathered courtside at Madison Square Garden for Game 4 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs. Taylor Swift, Timothée Chalamet, Adam Sandler, Spike Lee, Ben Stiller, and other prominent entertainment figures were in attendance to watch the high-profile matchup.

The Knicks delivered a dramatic performance, mounting a remarkable comeback to defeat the Spurs 107-106. The 29-point turnaround marked the largest comeback in NBA Finals history. With the victory, the Knicks took a 3-1 series lead in the best-of-seven matchup.

cards.headline: Kenny Loggins and Kevin Bacon Perform Footloose on Tonight Show
cards.teaser: Singer Kenny Loggins and actor Kevin Bacon performed a medley of Loggins' hits using classroom instruments on The Tonight Show.
cards.body:
Kenny Loggins and Kevin Bacon reunited on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to perform a medley of Loggins' greatest hits. The performance featured classroom instruments and included the iconic song "Footloose."

Bacon starred in the 1984 film Footloose, which launched Loggins' hit song to fame. The Tonight Show performance brought together the actor and musician for a nostalgic celebration of their connection to the classic track.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Performs The Cure on Jimmy Kimmel Live
cards.teaser: Singer Olivia Rodrigo performed her song The Cure on Jimmy Kimmel Live and discussed her childhood aspiration to work as a babysitter.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live, where she performed her song The Cure. During the show, host Jimmy Kimmel offered the singer an opportunity to fulfill a long-held dream of working as a babysitter.

Rodrigro discussed her childhood interest in babysitting during the interview segment. The appearance showcased new music from the singer while also exploring personal interests from her youth.

cards.headline: Teacher Performs Duet with Ed Sheeran After Canceling Holiday
cards.teaser: A teacher named Lianne Kaye abandoned her planned holiday to perform a duet with singer Ed Sheeran.
cards.body:
Lianne Kaye, a teacher, canceled her vacation plans to perform alongside Ed Sheeran. She described the experience of singing with the artist as honestly unbelievable.

Kaye made the decision to forgo her holiday when the opportunity to duet with Sheeran arose. The performance represented an unexpected chance for the teacher to share the stage with the popular British singer-songwriter.

hero.headline: Key U.S. spy authority nears expiration as lawmakers warn of national security risk
hero.teaser: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act could lapse on Friday, threatening intelligence operations.
hero.body:
One of America's most powerful spy authorities is nearing an unprecedented lapse, threatening to plunge intelligence agencies and telecommunications companies into legal uncertainty if allowed to expire on Friday. Members in both parties are warning that an expiration of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act could jeopardize U.S. national security.

Section 702 feeds more than half of the president's daily briefing and has been credited with helping thwart terror plots and other national security threats. The looming expiration adds pressure to lawmakers already dealing with uncertainty in the intelligence community.

cards.headline: U.S. conducts second night of airstrikes on Iran
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military launched strikes on Iran for the second consecutive evening on Wednesday, escalating military operations against Tehran. U.S. officials said the intent was to pressure Iran to sign a deal, though the strikes also carry a risk of further military escalation.

U.S. officials said they expected an Iranian response, possibly targeting U.S. bases, as happened on Tuesday. Tehran announced Wednesday night that its military had targeted the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet in Bahrain with drones in response to the latest American strikes, though it was not immediately clear whether the attack had struck its target.

The strikes mark a significant intensification of military action between the two nations. The two-night campaign represents the most direct U.S. military action against Iranian territory in recent years, raising questions about whether the situation will continue to escalate or whether the pressure will bring Iran to the negotiating table.

The dual-pronged approach by U.S. officials—conducting military strikes while simultaneously stating they aim to achieve a diplomatic agreement—reflects the tension between coercive tactics and the desire to avoid a broader regional conflict. The strikes come at a time when U.S. forces maintain a significant presence in the Middle East, including the 5th Fleet headquarters in Bahrain.

The situation continues to develop as both nations assess the impacts of the latest exchanges. U.S. officials indicated they are monitoring for further Iranian responses while maintaining their stated objective of reaching a negotiated settlement.

cards.headline: Trump's intelligence nominee scrambles renewal talks for spy tool
cards.teaser: Bill Pulte's appointment has complicated efforts to renew FISA 702 as lawmakers question his lack of experience.
cards.body:
President Trump's choice of Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community has scrambled talks to renew a spy tool known as FISA 702. Lawmakers in both parties have been vocal about his lack of national security experience and role as a Trump loyalist.

The appointment comes as Congress faces a deadline to renew the surveillance authority. Pulte's selection has raised concerns among members about the future direction of U.S. intelligence operations and whether he possesses the expertise needed to oversee the nation's spy agencies.

cards.headline: Incoming intelligence chief sought early departure of predecessor
cards.teaser: Bill Pulte told Tulsi Gabbard her last day was Tuesday, despite her announcement of a month-end departure.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte, Trump's pick to lead the intelligence community, called Tulsi Gabbard on Tuesday to tell her it was her last day as director of national intelligence. Gabbard had previously announced plans to leave at month's end, not immediately. She requested confirmation directly from the president or White House before accepting the abrupt departure.

The confrontation reflects broader tensions over Pulte's controversial appointment. Trump has instructed Pulte to execute an "immediate and needed downsizing" of the intelligence director's office. The transition has drawn criticism from lawmakers concerned that installing a presidential loyalist will undermine a bipartisan agreement to renew surveillance law authorities set to expire.

cards.headline: Trump urges Congress to pass $350 billion reconciliation bill
cards.teaser: The president called on Republicans to advance a third reconciliation package including the Save America Act.
cards.body:
President Trump on Wednesday called on Republicans in Congress to immediately pass a $350 billion reconciliation bill that includes the Save America Act. He emphasized the urgency of the measure, which he stated was requested by the Department of Defense.

Trump is pushing for the package to encompass both increased Pentagon funding and an elections overhaul as part of the GOP's next party-line legislative effort on Capitol Hill.

cards.headline: House Democrats struggle with campaign committee dues payments
cards.teaser: More than half of House Democrats had paid less than 50% of expected dues as of early April.
cards.body:
More than half of House Democrats had paid less than 50% of their expected dues to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee as of the beginning of April, with an average payment rate of 47%, according to a member dues report. Nearly 30 members who are not in battleground districts had paid nothing at all.

The low payment rates come as House Democrats threaten to withhold their dues to the DCCC unless it stops intervening in primaries. While not the committee's only source of income, member dues represent a significant funding stream for the party's campaign arm.

cards.headline: Agriculture secretary rejects screwworm vaccine proposal
cards.teaser: Brooke Rollins responded to Senator Chuck Grassley's urging to develop a vaccine for the parasite infestation.
cards.body:
Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley urged Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to create a vaccine for New World screwworms on Wednesday after the parasite infestation returned to the U.S. for the first time in 60 years. Grassley said he had spoken to Rollins about developing a vaccine for screwworms months before the recent outbreak in Texas.

Rollins knocked down the suggestion during the exchange. The outbreak has raised concerns about agricultural impacts as the parasite, which had been eradicated from the U.S. six decades ago, has now reappeared.
